title: Loops + Functions
summary: Call functions inside loops — this is where functions become genuinely powerful.

content.title: The Combination
content.summary: Calling a function inside a loop repeats the whole action automatically.
content.body:
You know loops repeat code. You know functions are reusable actions. Combine them:

def jump():
    print("Legs bend...")
    print("Jump!")
    print("Landing!")

for i in range(3):
    jump()

Output:
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!
Legs bend...
Jump!
Landing!

Three full jump actions — from just two lines of calling code.

content.title: Passing the Loop Variable
content.summary: Pass i into a function to make each call slightly different.
content.body:
You can pass i into the function so each round is labelled:

def battle_round(round_number):
    print("--- Round", round_number, "---")
    print("You attack!")
    print("The enemy strikes back.")

for i in range(1, 4):
    battle_round(i)

Output:
--- Round 1 ---
You attack!
The enemy strikes back.
--- Round 2 ---
...

content.title: Why This Is Better Than a Big Loop
content.summary: If you want to change the battle action, you only update the function — not every loop.
content.body:
Imagine the battle action needs to change. Without functions, you'd edit the code inside every loop.

With functions, you update battle_round() once — and every loop call automatically gets the new version.

This is called separation of concerns: the loop decides how many times, the function decides what happens.

content.title: Multiple Functions in One Loop
content.summary: A loop can call several different functions in sequence, building complex repeated scenes.

editorPrompt: Write a function called dance_move(step) that prints two lines describing that step. Then use a loop to call it for steps 1 through 5.
starterCode:
# A labelled dance move
def dance_move(step):
    pass

# Loop through 5 steps
progressiveHints: Replace pass with two print lines. Use the step parameter: print("Step", step, "— spin!").
Add a second line for flair, like print("The crowd cheers!").
Write for i in range(1, 6): and call dance_move(i) inside it.
challenge: Add a second function called big_finish() that prints a grand finale message. After the loop ends, call big_finish() once.
